clue.text: Sulphur, within which noxious deposits neat

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a playful description of a baby's nappy (diaper), the thing in which messy deposits are made

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: sulphur, inside which foul-smelling deposits sit neat and undiluted.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPPY is British for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat in the sense of smart and trim is a synonym of snappy, as in a snappy dresser.

clue.text: Accident putting potato in drink

indicators.note: the potato word is placed inside the drink word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
mash is mashed potato

explanation.surface: Someone causes a mishap by dropping potato into a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-up is a crash, a violent accident, especially between vehicles.

clue.text: Prophet's spoken, which will be boring

indicators.note: spoken says the word for prophet is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an augur is a prophet or soothsayer; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A prophet's pronouncements turn out to be dull.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a drilling tool, so it is the thing that bores holes.

clue.text: Be wary of your heading into lottery the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the whole assembly is read backwards
into puts the short pieces inside the lottery word

parts.note: a toss-up is a matter of pure chance, a lottery
taken as written

indicators.note: heading picks the first letter of your

explanation.surface: Advice to be cautious about putting your head into a lottery that is going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' places the short pieces after the first two letters of the lottery word, and 'the wrong way' then turns the whole run round, so the reversed string is what goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act timidly and warily, avoiding commitment.

clue.text: Linen provides income, given charge

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, money one earns, as in making a fast buck
to ram is to charge at something

explanation.surface: A linen business brings in money, given what it charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a coarse stiffened linen or cotton cloth used in bookbinding and tailoring.

clue.text: 17 to dine in south London area, losing weight

indicators.note: the dining word goes inside what remains of the London district
losing says the weight word is taken out of the place name

parts.note: Brixton is a district of south London
a ton is a unit of weight
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone heads to eat in a south London district, while dieting.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is POTTER: the answer is Beatrix Potter, author of Peter Rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrix Potter was the children's author, so she is one famous person with that surname.

clue.text: Tease husks from seeds

definitions.meaning: to banter with or mock someone playfully
the husks threshed away from grain

explanation.definitionFit: Chaff means both light-hearted teasing banter and the discarded husks of corn.

clue.text: Strong boy held up by result of previous failure

indicators.note: held says the exam word holds the boy inside it

parts.note: a resit is an exam retaken after failing

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the boy's name reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Neil is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy kept back to retake an exam after failing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' turns the boy upwards before 'held' wraps him. A resit is a British term for retaking a failed exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilient people are tough and able to recover, so strong is a fair synonym.

clue.text: 17 to continuously make money

parts.note: to mint is to make coins
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep making money without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is POTTER: Minton is a famous Staffordshire pottery firm, founded by Thomas Minton, a potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Minton was an English potter whose name became a celebrated brand of china.

clue.text: Huge car part

definitions.meaning: very large, as in a ... crop
the bar at the front or back of a vehicle that absorbs impact

explanation.definitionFit: Bumper is both an adjective for exceptionally large and the protective bar on a car.

clue.text: Barking Argonauts bark

indicators.note: barking means mad in British slang, so the letters go crazy

explanation.surface: Jason's crew of Argonauts have gone mad and are barking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like a dog's noise but is tree bark.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura is the aromatic bark of a South American tree, used to flavour bitters.

clue.text: Crime of priesticide?

parts.note: a made-up word for murdering a clergyman; drop the first letter of a word for that clergyman and what is left is a crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: A mock-legal term for the offence of murdering a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for a country clergyman, minus its P, gives the fire-raising crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: 17's trouble

definitions.meaning: the first name of the boy wizard who shares the surname at 17

explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter is the boy wizard, and to harry means to harass or trouble.

clue.text: Spooner's battled against disease, such a case

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: battled means fought
polio is a disease

explanation.surface: Someone fought hard against a disease, in just such a case.
explanation.walkthrough: FOUGHT POLIO with initial sounds swapped is heard as PORT FOLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for papers or drawings.

clue.text: What's expected to threaten the mayor's place

parts.note: par is the expected standard, as in golf
to lour is to look threatening, like a dark sky

explanation.surface: A predictable threat against the mayor's position.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor's parlour is the official reception room of a British mayor.

clue.text: Rhizome excessively climbing, way into outcrop

indicators.note: into puts the pieces inside the outcrop word

parts.note: an outcrop is a rock formation

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: too means excessively
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A plant root grows wildly up, making its way into a rocky outcrop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads upwards, so the word for excessively is turned before going into the outcrop with the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootstock is an underground stem, the same thing as a rhizome.

clue.text: Invader of Greece gaining pleasure by himself in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat says the pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: sex as a pleasure
himself can mean the master or king of a house; rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Greek invader enjoys himself privately while his army falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: SEXREX read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes was the Persian king who invaded Greece in 480 BC.

clue.text: Decree nisi almost wrecked home

indicators.note: wrecked says the letters are broken up and rearranged
almost drops the final letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A provisional divorce order nearly wrecks a family home.
explanation.walkthrough: A decree nisi is the provisional stage of a British divorce. DECREENIS, with the last letter gone, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling, someone's home.

clue.text: Waste time giving little money to animal

parts.note: p is a penny, a small amount of money
an otter is an animal

explanation.surface: Dawdling while handing small change to a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter is to idle about doing trivial things, wasting time.

clue.text: Dress design, lining split

indicators.note: the design word lines the inside of the split word

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
an aim is a design or intention

explanation.surface: A dress pattern whose lining has split.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old word for clothing, dress.

clue.text: Talk of silicon implants where "more room up top" announced?

indicators.note: talk of says the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: silicone implants come from a bust op, a breast enlargement operation

explanation.surface: Chatter about breast implants, promising more room up top.
explanation.walkthrough: On a double-decker bus, a conductor at the stop might announce there is more room on the upper deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus stop is where passengers might hear that seats remain upstairs on a double-decker.

clue.text: Blow instrument around noon

indicators.note: the instrument word goes around the letter for noon

parts.note: a bugle is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: Someone blows a brass instrument around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like playing a horn but is the verb meaning to botch.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow a chance is to bungle it, mess it up.

clue.text: Own crew on ship

parts.note: a posse is a gang or crew
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A crew on board a ship of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess is to own something.

clue.text: Busybody leader lacking leadership captured by uprising of Napoleon

indicators.note: the shortened leader word is held inside the reversed pig
in a down clue, uprising means read upwards

parts.note: Napoleon is the pig who rules in Orwell's Animal Farm

indicators.note: lacking leadership drops the first letter

parts.note: a boss is a leader

explanation.surface: A meddling leader is overthrown in a revolt against Napoleon.
explanation.walkthrough: BOSS without its first letter is OSS; PIG upwards gives GIP, which holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip is a person who spreads rumours, a busybody.

clue.text: Old book on pub crawl addiction

parts.note: a session is a long bout of drinking

explanation.surface: An old book about a pub crawl describes an addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a compulsive fixation, close to an addiction.

clue.text: 17's horse carrying small figure, old bird

indicators.note: the horse carries the figure inside it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
V is the Roman numeral five, a small number
avis is Latin, an old language, for bird

explanation.surface: A horse carrying a small figure along with an old bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is POTTER: Steve Davis is a snooker champion, and snooker players pot balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Davis was a great snooker player, and potting balls is the game's aim.

clue.text: See 23
Half-doubtful misgivings, which may suggest hostility or peace

definitions.text: which may suggest hostility or peace

indicators.note: doubtful says those letters are uncertain in order and rearranged
half takes every other letter of misgivings

explanation.surface: Half-hearted misgivings about a gesture that can mean war or peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of misgivings are IGVNS, rearranged. In Britain the V-sign palm inward is rude; palm outward means victory or peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-finger V-sign can be insulting or a sign of peace depending on how it is made.

clue.text: 17 finds whales in Kent

indicators.note: the whales word sits inside the region

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, SE
a pod is a group of whales

explanation.surface: A potter discovers whales off the Kent coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is POTTER: Josiah Spode was an English potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spode was a Staffordshire potter whose name became a famous china brand.

clue.text: Force of severe gale about Beaufort's ultimate after windy gale rose

indicators.note: after puts the force section behind the rearranged gale
windy says the second gale is blown into a new order
the force number goes about the last letter

parts.note: a severe gale is force nine on the Beaufort scale

indicators.note: ultimate picks the last letter of Beaufort's

explanation.surface: A weather report about severe gale force on the Beaufort scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a verb but is the flower; 'windy' scrambles the second gale into EGLA, and Beaufort force nine is a severe gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose.

clue.text: Menace collecting fine, one the most confined

indicators.note: the menace word collects the other pieces inside

parts.note: a pest is a menace
OK means fine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nuisance collects a fine, one of the most cramped.
explanation.definitionFit: Poky means cramped and small, so pokiest is the most confined.

clue.text: 17 strayed from right to left

indicators.note: from right to left says the word is read backwards

parts.note: strayed in the moral sense means sinned

explanation.surface: A potter went astray, from the right side to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is POTTER: Dennis Potter was a British TV dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis Potter wrote The Singing Detective, so he is a well-known bearer of the surname.
